raw_text:
Thanks — I’ll give you a progressive, 12-week strength-focused program tailored to a 27‑year‑old male beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull‑up bar. The plan emphasizes safe progressive overload using bodyweight, simple periodisation, daily structure, mobility and recovery, and basic nutrition guidance for strength/beginner muscle gain. Each week lists sessions, exercises, sets/reps/tempo, and progression cues.

Overall structure (phases)
- Weeks 1–4 (Foundation): build movement quality, joint resilience, work capacity, and establish baseline strength. Focus on full‑body, higher frequency (3–4 sessions/week).
- Weeks 5–8 (Strength Build): increase intensity via mechanical progression (harder variations), lower reps, add more focused pulling and pushing volume. 3 sessions/week (full‑body) with slightly heavier effort per set.
- Weeks 9–12 (Peak Strength / Complexity): push harder variations, focus on controlled, low‑rep sets and added difficulty (paused reps, slower eccentrics, single‑leg/arm work). 3 sessions/week with one optional light technique or conditioning day.

Assumptions and safety notes
- Client is medically cleared for exercise. Teach proper hinge/squat/push/pull mechanics before loading.
- Doorway pull‑up bar should be secure; teach scapular pullups and negatives if full pull‑up not yet possible.
- Rest 60–120 sec between strength sets (longer for heavier sets). Warm up 5–10 minutes before each session (see Warm‑up section).
- If an exercise causes pain (sharp or joint), stop and regress to easier variation.
- Progress each week either by adding reps, sets, improving range of motion, slowing tempo (control), adding pauses, or advancing the variation.

Weekly frequency
- Weeks 1–4: 4 sessions/week (3 full‑body strength + 1 mobility/conditioning or extra skill day)
- Weeks 5–12: 3 sessions/week (full‑body strength sessions A/B/C), with optional 4th active recovery/skill day.

Tempo notation: Eccentric/Isometric/Concentric (seconds). Example 3/1/1 = 3s lowering, 1s pause at bottom, 1s concentric.

Warm‑up (perform before every session; ~8–10 minutes)
- 2–3 minutes gentle cardio in place (marching, high knees, gentle jumping jacks if joints allow)
- Joint circles (neck, shoulders, hips, knees, ankles) 30s each
- Dynamic movements: hip hinges (10), world’s greatest stretch (5 per side), thoracic rotations (8 per side)
- Movement‑specific sets: 1–2 light sets of the first main exercise with easier variation (e.g., assisted squat to 8–10 reps)

Progression principles
- Aim to increase load/time under tension each week: add 1–3 reps per set until target rep range exceeded, then progress to harder variation or add an extra set.
- If not ready for full pull‑ups, progress through scapular pulls → active hangs → negatives → band assisted (if no band, use chair/foot assistance) → full pull‑up.
- For push and squat, progress from wall/box/assisted to full range and then to more difficult variations (elevated single‑leg or slower eccentrics).

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation (4 days/week)
Goal: build movement patterns, base strength, conditioning, and posterior chain.

Week 1 (4 sessions)
Session 1 (Full body A)
- Warm up
- Push: Incline push‑ups (hands on wall or elevated surface/bed) 3 x 8–12 (Tempo 2/0/1)
- Pull: Scapular pull‑ups (hang from bar, pull shoulder blades down/up) 4 x 6–8 (2/0/1)
- Legs: Box/Chair squats (sit to a chair, controlled) 3 x 10–12 (3/0/1)
- Hinge: Hip hinge/Good mornings (bodyweight) 3 x 10 (3/0/1)
- Core: Dead bug 3 x 8–10 per side
- Finisher: 60s plank x 2

Session 2 (Mobility/Conditioning)
- Mobility flow 15 min (hips, thoracic)
- Conditioning: 4 rounds, minimal rest — 30s jumping jacks / 30s bodyweight squats / 30s rest

Session 3 (Full body B)
- Warm up
- Push: Knee push‑ups 3 x 8–12 (2/0/1)
- Pull: Active hangs (dead hang with scapular control) 3 x 20–30s
- Legs: Reverse lunges (static) 3 x 8 per leg (2/0/1)
- Hinge: Single‑leg Romanian hinge to light touch chair (bodyweight) 3 x 6–8 each
- Core: Side plank 3 x 20–30s per side

Session 4 (Skill/recovery)
- Light practice: practice controlled negatives for pull‑ups: 4 x 3–5 negatives (3–5s lowering) or assisted pull‑ups
- 20 min yoga/mobility

Progression for Weeks 2–4
- Week 2: Slightly increase reps 1–2 per set and add 1 rep to isometric hangs; increase plank time +10s.
- Week 3: Move incline push‑ups lower (from wall to sofa edge), add an extra set to squats (4 x 10–12).
- Week 4: Attempt more challenging variations—full push‑ups for some sets if possible; add 1–2 scapular pull‑ups per set or start negatives (3–5s). Increase single‑leg hinge reps.

By end of week 4 target:
- 3–5 clean supported pull movements (scapular/active hang/short negative)
- 10–15 full range bodyweight squats for 3 sets
- 5–10 full push‑ups for at least 1–2 sets (if not, continue regressions)

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Strength Build (3 sessions/week)
Goal: increase mechanical difficulty, move toward unassisted pull‑ups and full push‑ups; introduce lower rep/higher intensity sets.

Session structure (A/B/C rotate; train Mon/Wed/Fri)
Session A
- Warm up
- Pull: Negative to partial pull‑up/assisted pull‑up 5 x 3–5 (5s eccentric or build concentric if possible)
- Push: Full push‑ups 4 x 6–10 (2/0/1). If not possible, do elevated push‑ups lower surface each week.
- Legs: Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on couch/chair) 4 x 6–8 per leg (3/0/1)
- Hinge: Glute bridge single‑leg progressions 3 x 8–10 each
- Core: Hollow holds 3 x 20–30s

Session B
- Warm up
- Pull: Australian/inverted rows using bar in low doorway setup or under table 4 x 8–12 (if safe). If not possible, do more negatives/scapular pull progressions.
- Push: Decline push‑ups (feet elevated) or archer push‑up progression 4 x 5–8 total
- Legs: Pistol squat box progression (single‑leg to box/chair) 4 x 5–8 per leg
- Core: Russian twist 3 x 12–16

Session C
- Warm up
- Pull: Attempt full pull‑ups for work sets: 5 sets of as many quality reps as possible (AMRAP) with 2–3 min rest. If none yet, do assisted to hit 6–8 reps.
- Push: Diamond or close‑grip push‑ups 4 x 6–10
- Legs: Reverse Nordic or deep slow eccentrics to a box 3 x 6–8
- Finisher: Tabata (20s on / 10s off) — bodyweight squats x 4 min

Progression notes Weeks 5–8
- Week 5: Use negatives or heavy assistance to perform 3–5 quality pull reps per set.
- Week 6: Shift some sets to attempted concentric pull‑ups; if 1–2 reps appear, keep negatives for remaining sets.
- Week 7: Increase set intensity—aim for 5 sets of 3–6 challenging reps per pull/push movement.
- Week 8: If able, perform 3–5 full pull‑ups in sets; increase push‑up difficulty (narrower, declines) and increase single‑leg leg volume.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Peak Strength / Complexity (3 sessions/week + optional skill)
Goal: move toward low‑rep max strength, advanced bodyweight variations, increase time under tension for strength gains.

Session A (Strength heavy)
- Warm up
- Pull: Weighted (if no weight, add slow eccentrics and pauses): Pull‑ups 5 x 3–5 with 3s eccentric, 1s pause at top. If still building, do long negatives and hold top.
- Push: Archer or pseudo planche push‑ups (lean forward) 5 x 4–6 (tempo 3/0/1)
- Legs: Elevated single‑leg squats/pistol 5 x 4–6 per leg
- Core: Hanging knee raises / tuck hangs 4 x 8–12

Session B (Volume + strength)
- Warm up
- Pull: Close‑grip chin‑up variation 4 x 6–8 or slow negatives
- Push: Slow tempo decline push‑ups 4 x 6–8 (5/1/1)
- Legs: Slow tempo Bulgarian split squat 4 x 6–8 per leg
- Accessory: Reverse hypers (glute raises off couch) 3 x 12

Session C (Power/Control + conditioning)
- Warm up
- Pull: Explosive pull attempts or fast concentric negatives—5 x 3 (focus on speed up)
- Push: Plyo push‑ups (if safe) 4 x 5–8 or clap progression, or fast concentric push ups
- Legs: Jump lunges / squat jumps 4 x 6–10 (or slow eccentrics if impact not desired)
- Finisher: EMOM 10 — alternating movements: minute 1 plank 45s, minute 2 bodyweight rows 8–10, etc.

Progression Weeks 9–12
- Week 9: Aim for clean 3–5 rep sets on primary lifts (pulls/pushes/single‑leg squats).
- Week 10: Increase time under tension via slower eccentrics and 1–2s pauses at weak points.
- Week 11: Peak week — target heavier single‑leg/pull variations; reduce total volume slightly and increase intensity.
- Week 12: Test week — measure 1–3 rep max for pull‑ups (max reps), maximum full push‑ups in one set, single‑leg pistol clean reps. This week reduce accessory volume and focus on top sets and recovery.

Sample week‑by‑week quick outline (weeks 1–12)
- Week 1–4: 4 sessions per week, follow Week 1 template with gradual weekly progressions described.
- Week 5: Start 3x/week A/B/C with moderate reps as above.
- Week 6: Increase reps/sets as client adapts.
- Week 7: Shift toward lower rep intensity sets on key lifts.
- Week 8: Solidify multiple unassisted pull‑ups or consistent 3–5 rep sets.
- Week 9–11: Increase difficulty of variations, focus on 3–6 rep strength sets and single‑leg emphasis.
- Week 12: Testing week — reduce volume, test 1–3RM style strength measures (or maximum reps for bodyweight lifts).

Example progression markers to track
- Ability to do 5 strict pull‑ups (unassisted)
- 3 sets of 10 full push‑ups
- Single‑leg squat to full depth for 6 consistent reps per leg
- Plank 90s, hanging knee raise 12 reps

Recovery, sleep and deloading
- Sleep: aim 7–9 hours nightly.
- Deload: If client feels overly fatigued at start of week 9, insert a deload week by reducing volume by ~40% (fewer sets, lighter progressions).
- Active recovery day: light walk, mobility, foam rolling, and extra sleep/hydration.

Nutrition guidance (basic for strength/hypertrophy)
- Calories: slight surplus for muscle gain. For a 27‑year‑old male beginner, a simple starting guideline is maintenance + 200–300 kcal/day. Adjust based on weight change (aim ~0.25–0.5% bodyweight gain/week).
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day. If weight unknown, target 140–180 g/day for many average‑sized males; at minimum 0.8–1 g per lb of body weight.
- Carbs: emphasize around training (pre/post) for performance—moderate intake (3–5 g/kg).
- Fat: make up remaining calories, minimum ~20–25% of total calories.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day baseline; more if sweating heavily.
- Feeding around sessions: small carb + protein snack 60–90 min pre workout and 20–60 min post workout (e.g., yogurt and banana, tuna sandwich, protein shake).

Coaching cues and technique priorities
- Pulls: think elbow back; engage lats first; scapular retraction before pulling.
- Pushes: braced core, shoulder blades stable, full range with controlled descent.
- Squats: knees track toes, sit back, maintain an upright torso appropriate to variation.
- Hinges: push hips back, soft knees, chest up.
- Breathing: inhale on descent, exhale on concentric push; brace core.

Optional equipment you can advise client to obtain (low cost, optional)
- A light resistance band for pull assistance and mobility (~$10–15)
- A suspension trainer or extra door anchor for rows if desired
- Small ankle weight or backpack (for progressive loading later)

Example Month-by-month measurable outcomes
- Month 1: consistent movement patterns, improved endurance in bodyweight sets, first strict negative pull‑ups/active hangs for 30–60s.
- Month 2: achieve multiple sets of 3–5 pull‑up reps (or consolidate assisted to 6–8), full push‑ups for multiple sets, stronger single‑leg control.
- Month 3: 5+ strict pull‑ups in one set or 3–5 rep max at high intensity, confident single‑leg squat strength, visible improvements in push/pull numbers.

If you want
- I can convert this into a printable week‑by‑week table for the client.
- I can give specific sample meals and calorie targets if you tell me his weight/height and goals (fat loss, gain, or maintain).
- I can provide short video cue descriptions or a staged progressions list for each exercise.

Would you like that additional detail (bodyweight progressions visual list or daily printable plan)?
